theory.title: Exercise 2.2.3: Keywords with Arguments
theory.content:
🔌 Making Keywords Flexible

MENTOR-9: "PROTO-7, imagine a wrench that only fits ONE bolt. Useless! Arguments are like adjustable wrenches - they adapt to different situations."

"Instead of 'Check Power' and 'Check Sensors' as separate keywords, create ONE flexible 'Check System' that accepts WHICH system to check."

⚙️ What are Keyword Arguments?

Arguments - Parameters that keywords accept for flexible behavior

  • ✅ Flexibility - One keyword handles multiple scenarios
  • ✅ DRY Principle - Don't Repeat Yourself
  • ✅ Maintainability - Change logic in one place
  • ✅ Expressiveness - Keywords read like natural language

Without Arguments (Rigid):

Check Power System
    Log    Checking power

Check Sensor System
    Log    Checking sensors

With Arguments (Flexible):

Check System
    [Arguments]    ${system}
    Log    Checking ${system}

📝 Keyword Arguments Syntax

*** Keywords ***
Greet Person
    [Arguments]    ${name}
    Log    Hello ${name}!

Add Numbers
    [Arguments]    ${a}    ${b}
    ${result}=    Evaluate    ${a} + ${b}
    Log    Result: ${result}

Calling with Arguments:

*** Test Cases ***
Greeting Test
    Greet Person    Alice
    Greet Person    Bob

Math Test
    Add Numbers    5    3

📋 Keyword Arguments Rules

  • 🔹 [Arguments]: Must be FIRST line inside keyword
  • 🔹 Syntax: [Arguments] ${arg1} ${arg2}
  • 🔹 Spacing: 4 spaces between arguments
  • 🔹 Naming: Use descriptive ${variable} names
  • 🔹 Passing: Arguments passed after keyword name

🎯 Your Task

Create a flexible 'Check System' keyword that accepts the system name as an argument. Call it three times with different systems!
